market_context: United States/general English; handling raw chicken and preventing kitchen cross-contamination
title: Should you wash chicken before cooking?

seo.title: Should you wash raw chicken before cooking?
seo.meta_description: No. Washing raw chicken does not make it safer and can spread bacteria around the sink and kitchen. Cook poultry to 165 °F instead.
seo.search_intent: Learn why USDA advises against washing raw chicken and what to do instead for safe handling.

excerpt: USDA advises against washing raw poultry. Running water can splash bacteria from chicken onto the sink, faucet, counters, utensils or ready-to-eat food. Safe handling and cooking to at least 165 °F in the thickest part are more effective than rinsing.
content_html:
Running water over raw chicken does not sterilize it. USDA advises against washing poultry because splashes can spread bacteria around the kitchen.

Why washing can increase risk

Water hitting raw poultry can carry microorganisms to the sink, faucet, counters, utensils and nearby foods. The chicken may look cleaner while the kitchen becomes harder to keep clean.

Vinegar, lemon and salt water are not safety substitutes

Soaking or rinsing may be part of a recipe or family tradition, but it is not a reliable pathogen-control step. USDA states that rinsing, washing or soaking is unnecessary for safety.

Heat is the reliable control

Chicken should reach at least 165 °F (73.9 °C) in the thickest appropriate area, measured with a food thermometer.

What to do instead

  • Open the package without splashing raw juices.
  • If browning matters, pat the surface dry with disposable paper towels.
  • Wash hands with soap after handling raw chicken.
  • Clean and sanitize utensils and surfaces that contacted raw poultry.
  • Keep chicken and its juices away from ready-to-eat foods.

If you already washed it

You do not need to throw the chicken away. Clean and sanitize the sink, faucet, counters and anything reached by splashes, wash your hands and cook the chicken properly.

Bottom line

Do not wash chicken to make it safe. Prevent cross-contamination and use a thermometer during cooking.

faq.question: Does vinegar kill bacteria on raw chicken?
faq.answer: Not reliably enough to replace safe cooking. USDA does not recommend washing or soaking poultry for safety.

faq.question: Can I pat chicken dry?
faq.answer: Yes. Use disposable paper towel, discard it immediately and wash your hands afterward.

faq.question: What temperature should chicken reach?
faq.answer: At least 165 °F in the thickest part, measured with a food thermometer.
